chunks: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah b. Amer from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Abdullah b. al-Qasim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather from Ali (peace be upon them). He said:

Be more hopeful in that which you have no hope than in that which you have hope. For surely, Musa b. Imran (peace be upon him) went to fetch fire for his family, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke to him and he returned as a prophet. The queen of Saba came out and accepted Islam with Sulayman (peace be upon him). The magicians of Pharaoh went out seeking glory for Pharaoh, yet they returned as believers.

key_terms.ترجو: Hope -- the central theme of placing trust in Allah's unexpected blessings
key_terms.سحرة فرعون: Pharaoh's magicians -- who came to oppose Musa but ended up believing
key_terms.يقتبس: To fetch/seek fire -- Musa's mundane errand that led to prophethood

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about placing hope in the unexpected?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a chain reaching Imam Ali (AS), encourages believers to place greater hope in the unexpected than the expected. It illustrates this through three Quranic examples: Musa went to find fire but received prophethood, the Queen of Sheba set out on a diplomatic mission but found faith, and Pharaoh's magicians sought to glorify tyranny but returned as believers. The teaching was particularly relevant in the context of early Islamic society where believers faced uncertainty about their future.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from `Abdullah b. al-Qasim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather from `Ali (as). He said:

Be more hopeful in that which you have no hope than in that which you have hope. Surely, Musa b. `Imran (as) went to fetch some fire for his family, yet Allah spoke to him and he returned [to them] as a prophet. The queen of Saba’ came out and accepted Islam with Sulayman (as). The magicians of Pharaoh went out seeking glory for Pharaoh, yet they returned as believers.
